title: Western Wanderings
subtitle: A Record of Travel in the Evening Land

history.note: A printer’s error of a dropped or transposed letter marked and corrected: “ocasional” for “occasional”.

summary: An English traveller’s account of a journey through North America in the early 1870s (the book gives no year; it reports events of 1872 and 1873 as recent). He crossed the Atlantic to New York, went by way of Niagara and Chicago to Omaha, and took the Union Pacific Railroad to Salt Lake City and on to Virginia City. In California he rode the stage-coaches to the Big Trees and the Yosemite Valley and spent time in San Francisco. He then travelled north by Mount Shasta, camped out, and visited the lava beds where the Modoc War had just been fought, with an account of the war. He went on through Oregon to the Columbia River, Puget Sound, and Victoria, up the Fraser River, to Nanaimo, and back to San Francisco and the Geysers. The last chapter gives his general remarks on the West.
